ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Rapidly enlarging upper-lip swelling after eating prawn soup (~19:00 today).  
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Swelling noticed ~30 min after ingestion; continues to enlarge.  
  • Now reports breathing difficulty and dizziness.  
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat: subjectively “can’t breathe that well”; no voice change reported.  
  • Oral/facial: progressive upper-lip swelling; no tongue or uvular swelling mentioned.  
  • No reports of dysphagia, odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor, ear pain, or neck swelling.  
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Age ~6 yrs: severe peanut reaction requiring hospital care and injection (likely adrenaline).  
  • ~1 yr ago: facial swelling and breathing difficulty after late-night Chinese meal; self-managed, details unclear.  
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Peanut allergy (documented).  
  • Asthma: Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Intermittent antihistamine use for allergies (type/dose not documented).  
  • No epinephrine auto-injector currently.  
- Social context:
  • Initially alone; mother now present and assisting.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Patient reports progressive upper-lip edema; no visual confirmation of tongue/face swelling documented.  
- Airway/breathing: Subjective dyspnea; no stridor or wheeze documented.  
- Mental status: Alert but dizzy.  
- Vitals/exam: Not recorded.  
- Accompaniment: Mother present.

Assessment:
- Suspected acute anaphylactic reaction precipitated by shellfish (prawn) ingestion in a patient with known severe food allergies (peanuts) and prior anaphylaxis history—evidenced by rapid onset mucosal swelling, respiratory difficulty, and systemic dizziness.

Plan:
- Immediate actions:
  • Advised/initiated emergency call to 999 for ambulance transport—“suspected anaphylactic reaction.”  
  • Instructed patient to take available oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.  
- Safety instructions:
  • Mother to remain with patient continuously until ambulance arrival.  
  • Monitor for worsening breathing, throat tightness, voice change, or loss of consciousness; if occurs, inform EMS dispatcher immediately.  
- Follow-up:
  • After hospital discharge, patient to contact clinic for review.  
  • Arrange ENT/allergy referral for formal evaluation, confirm shellfish allergy, and provide education.  
  • Prescribe adrenaline auto-injector and teach proper use.  
  • Reinforce strict avoidance of peanuts, shellfish, and any identified allergens; carry antihistamine and auto-injector at all times.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: objective vital signs, detailed airway exam, specific antihistamine name/dose, confirmation of epinephrine auto-injector availability, full allergy list, asthma control assessment.  
• Internal conflicts: Unclear whether chest tightness present (“not sure”).  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; no major inaudible sections noted.
